record.paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
record.original_question: Can one classify all quantum limits of eigenfunctions of a polygonal billiard?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 55 (J. Marklof ). Classify all quantum limits of the eigenfunctions of a polygonal billiard.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a polygonal billiard, i.e., a compact connected planar domain whose boundary $\partial P$ is a finite union of line segments. Consider the Dirichlet (or Neumann) Laplacian $-\Delta$ on $P$, whose spectrum consists of eigenvalues $0 < \lambda_1 \le \lambda_2 \le \cdots \to \infty$ with corresponding $L^2$-normalized real eigenfunctions $\varphi_n$ satisfying $-\Delta \varphi_n = \lambda_n \varphi_n$. For each $n$, lift $\varphi_n$ to a distribution on the unit cotangent bundle $S^*P$ via its microlocal lift, obtaining a probability measure $\mu_n$ on $S^*P$. A probability measure $\mu$ on $S^*P$ is called a quantum limit if there is a subsequence $n_k \to \infty$ such that $\mu_{n_k} \to \mu$ weakly. Every quantum limit is invariant under the billiard flow on $S^*P$.

Problem: Classify all quantum limits of eigenfunctions of an arbitrary polygonal billiard $P$. That is, characterize the set of all such weak-$*$ limit measures, both for rational polygons (those whose interior angles are rational multiples of $\pi$) and for general polygons.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open in full generality. Marklof and Rudnick (2012) established quantum ergodicity for rational polygons, showing a density-one subsequence of eigenfunctions equidistributes in configuration space, but a complete classification of all quantum limits — including possible exceptional (scarring) sequences and the situation for general (irrational) polygons — has not been achieved. Related work on the Šeba billiard (Kurlberg–Ueberschär, Hillairet et al.) exhibits non-uniform quantum limits ("superscars") in closely related models, indicating the full classification is subtle and unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Around Quantum Ergodicity (Dyatlov)
status_evidence.snippet: Marklof–Rudnick proved quantum ergodicity for rational polygons; the structure of all quantum limits beyond the density-one subsequence is not classified.
status_evidence.claim: Only quantum ergodicity (density-one equidistribution) is known for rational polygons; complete classification of quantum limits is open.

status_evidence.title: Superscars in the Šeba billiard (Kurlberg–Ueberschär)
status_evidence.snippet: Exhibits non-uniform quantum limits (superscars) in a related billiard model, demonstrating that quantum limits in polygonal-type systems can be highly non-trivial.
status_evidence.claim: Related models show non-Liouville quantum limits, indicating no complete classification is known for polygonal billiards.

status_evidence.title: J. Marklof: Eigenfunctions of polygonal billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Recent talk discussing eigenfunctions of polygonal billiards, indicating ongoing research activity.
status_evidence.claim: The topic remains an area of active research without a complete classification.
